description:
Canonical reference (crate-jmap-mail-server/src/memory.rs:110-114) uses:

    objects: HashMap<(&'static str, String), HashMap<Id, serde_json::Value>>,
    states: HashMap<(&'static str, String), u64>,
    change_log: HashMap<(&'static str, String), Vec<ChangeEntry>>,

Six siblings still use HashMap<(String, String), _>:

  crate-jmap-calendars-server/src/memory.rs:124-128
  crate-jmap-chat-server/src/memory.rs:81-85
  crate-jmap-contacts-server/src/memory.rs:115-119
  crate-jmap-sharing-server/src/memory.rs:81-85
  crate-jmap-tasks-server/src/memory.rs:121-125
  (crate-jmap-filenode-server/src/memory.rs uses a different shape — not in scope)

The type_name comes from O::TYPE_NAME which is &'static str on the JmapObject trait. Every read site in the 6 siblings does type_name.to_owned() solely to fit the key shape — ~28 needless String allocations across the affected files (grep '.to_owned\(\), account_id\.to_owned\(\)' confirms). Canonical mail-server got it right; the siblings drifted.

Workspace AGENTS.md 'Canonical Templates' makes this a propagation finding, not an opinion: per the rule, siblings cookie-cut from the canonical and any divergence is a regression of the cookie-cutter intent.

Why P2 (not P3): the canonical's chosen shape is a deliberate idiom improvement that the siblings missed; the propagation rule explicitly classifies this as a regression to fix; the fix is mechanical (sed s/HashMap<(String, String)/HashMap<(&'static str, String)/ and update get/entry sites to drop type_name.to_owned()).
title: P2: MemoryBackend HashMap key type cookie-cutter drift — 6 siblings use (String, String); canonical mail-server uses (&'static str, String)
